text.p: Mexican police arrested a prominent peasant leader in the troubled southwestern state of Guerrero on Monday, the latest left-wing peasant activist rounded up in recent weeks.

State police said in a statement they had arrested Bertoldo Martinez Cruz, leader of the UOSS peasant group, on charges of sedition and robbery. The UOSS is an umbrella organisation for leftist peasant groups in the impoverished state.

Police arrested the leader of another local peasant group, Benigno Guzman, last week on similar charges and said he was the head of a feared Marxist guerrilla group, the Popular Revolutionary Amry (EPR).
Monday's police statement made no reference to the EPR, a group which first appeared last year and has killed about 30 people in attacks on police and army units.

Guzman has denied charges that he is an EPR leader and on Monday condemned the arrest of Martinez, telling reporters from his jail cell that the government was fabricating charges against peasant leaders in order to stop their activities.

Police said Martinez was being charged with sedition for storming the city hall of Tlacoachistlahuaca, a tiny village some 180 miles (300 km) south of Mexico City, in late 1995 with a handful of supporters.
